findings.title: The new B reservation/protection wrapper can probe the filesystem after an ACK refusal
findings.trigger: In reserve_source_companion or protect_source_companion, the family writer operation succeeds and Connection::close succeeds, but WriterCloseObserver::after_close returns a standalone non-Cleanup cause, such as invalid("ack refused"). The source RO snapshot is still enclosing that writer.
findings.consequence: The family writer's failure is returned into source_companion_snapshot, which uses the ordinary interpreting reader. That reader closes B's source connection successfully and then calls database.snapshot() before returning the failure. Thus there is a subsequent filesystem/sidecar probe after the refused ACK, contrary to the stated stop-on-failed-acknowledgement contract and W3. This does not assert that a further commit occurs or that an actual failed SQLite close is ignored.

evidence.fact: reserve_source_companion performs bare.finish_writer inside the callback of source_companion_snapshot.
writer_close_result returns a single observer fault directly when the operation and actual close succeeded; that fault need not be Cause::Cleanup.
The ordinary reader propagates Cleanup early, but a plain callback error reaches the concluding database.snapshot().
An existing read_cancellable_strict entry explicitly suppresses the concluding filesystem probe after any callback failure while retaining the mandatory real close.

findings.correction: Use the existing strict nested-reader failure policy for source_companion_snapshot, or an equivalent explicit ACK-error propagation path that closes retained connections but performs no concluding SQL/FS probe. Retain positive-close/readback behavior on success. ROOT should qualify standalone ACK refusal separately from actual SQLite close failure when native work is authorized.
findings.provenance: Introduced in this proposal's new physical source-protection adapter.
findings.execution_status: SOURCE_REASONING_ONLY; dependent production lease integration remains unfinished

findings.title: Every first insertion of a companion deletion uses eight values for seven columns
findings.trigger: A closed companion contains at least one deletion whose scalar row is absent, as required for a genuine new B Staging-to-Ready publication. insert_new_rows reaches insert_exact for that deletion.
findings.consequence: DELETION_INSERT names seven columns but supplies VALUES(?1,...,?8). deletion_values produces seven values. The insertion statement is invalid and the new publication cannot complete. In the managed B path, earlier mutations must roll back, so this is a deterministic publication failure rather than evidence of committed partial data. Exact-row replay can skip executing the invalid statement and therefore does not demonstrate that first publication works.

evidence.fact: Each new deletion executes DELETION_INSERT through insert_exact.
deletion_values returns exactly companion_id, path, base_file_id, base_executable, base_manifest_id, reason and digest.
insert_exact executes the SQL only when the row is absent.
The newly added source publication path calls this primitive before claim/receipt publication.
The managed source path wraps the atom and rolls back operation failures before nested RO scopes close.

findings.correction: Make DELETION_INSERT's VALUES list match the seven declared columns and the seven-value projection. When ROOT authorizes execution, distinguish first insertion with a deletion from already-present replay in validation.
findings.provenance: Inherited unchanged from the 23-file predecessor and present in the cumulative candidate. It is reported because the newly delivered B publication directly depends on it; predecessor delivery was not treated as acceptance.
findings.execution_status: SOURCE_REASONING_ONLY; no SQL was prepared or executed

findings.title: The autonomous source-namespace reader accumulates all large root payloads before cross-group validation
findings.trigger: A family catalog contains many individually canonical source-companion roots and matching reservations. Each root can approach the 16 MiB per-root limit. retained_namespace reads and retains them all before returning to its admitted/terminal callers; those callers have not yet checked each root against its C group. Multiple such preliminary roots can reference one existing C group, so the earlier exact-journal row-count fence alone does not bound this collection.
findings.consequence: The Vec owns up to 4,096 SourceCompanionProtection values, each retaining its payload and manifest-ID collection. Payload retention alone can approach 64 GiB, with additional parsing/re-encoding temporaries. An oversized or ultimately invalid family can exhaust memory before the later group checks reject it. The existing destination-root walk explicitly streams one root at a time, but the new source-root prepass defeats that bound.

evidence.fact: SourceCompanionProtection owns payload: Vec<u8> and manifests: Vec<String>.
read_retained bounds a single payload at 16 MiB, materializes it, reconstructs it, and returns an owning protection value.
All source roots have already been collected before C-binding, U and member cross-checks begin.
The later destination-root loop explicitly avoids accumulating 4,096 large unions.
The terminal Ready interpreter also consumes the fully accumulated source-root vector.

findings.correction: Stream source roots through the caller's validation and retain only bounded identifiers needed to account for reservations, or preflight and enforce a conservative aggregate payload/manifest budget before materializing the vector. Do not rely on later C-group or global-count rejection to bound earlier allocation.
findings.provenance: Introduced by the new retained_namespace implementation.

checked_invariants.invariant: Complete exact private row, claim and mapping ownership, including capture coexistence
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported in the traced validators, subject to the publication failure in C13-CR-002; not runtime-qualified.
checked_invariants.reasoning: Bounded capture history is DATA, then terminal transition/receipt ownership and outgoing v2 rows are interpreted, and only then is the final capture proof produced. Extra headers/orphan scalars/unowned companion claims and content outside the capture/outgoing reference union are rejected. A shared FileId must retain the same mapping, while Accepted capture content and claims remain mandatory.

checked_invariants.invariant: Full publication/equality preserves outgoing companions without extending incoming ancestry
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported in the traced adapter and equality paths.
checked_invariants.reasoning: Companion proof participates in publication hashing and mutation equality. Outgoing validation starts from receipt.source_prefix and its original ancestry root; it does not make the outgoing receipt a parent or mutate frozen selectors.

checked_invariants.invariant: Descriptor-only preimages come from authenticated original descriptors; same FileId alternates remain distinct
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported in the concrete reconciliation path; full driver use remains an unfinished dependency.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The complete image adapter obtains a descriptor view from the private proof. Frozen mappings win over descriptors; a base/preimage without either refuses instead of using a recovery scalar. ManifestId, rather than FileId alone, keys the root union, with conflicting lengths rejected.

checked_invariants.invariant: Q_B is independently fixed from actual SQL projections plus the bounded canonical root; no quota growth or capture borrowing
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported in the derivation and B reservation paths.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The envelope charges reused mappings, actual header/scalars, claim, actual planned receipt and both terminal intent projections. A counting serializer and 19-digit sizing field bound the root before aggregate canonical encoding. Fixed remaining==Q_B is required; no B debit, top-up or quota mutation is introduced. The root-constructor bound does not cure the separate retained-namespace aggregate issue C13-CR-003.

checked_invariants.invariant: Global capacity includes absent B and C reservations, all existing reservations, CAS and journal charges; C remains the exact debit owner
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported in the traced B capacity and C validation paths.
checked_invariants.reasoning: B capacity adds both missing envelopes to complete family usage. Existing C reservation shape is checked there; C's independent validator retains quota-minus-durable-debit equality. B protection inserts only its reservation/root/membership and rejects B-owned exact journals.

checked_invariants.invariant: New C effects require full source context and a genuine fixed B reservation; legacy None paths remain strict
checked_invariants.assessment: Fail-closed seam supported; complete companion lease integration is explicitly unfinished.
checked_invariants.reasoning: New-companion installation/protection/reservation validators call require_source_envelope, bind plan/U and refuse absent B reservation. The complete proof's capture component is pointer-bound. The current legacy lease still supplies None and cannot be treated as a companion-capable driver.

checked_invariants.invariant: Both B/C roots precede either new receipt; B private rows wait for independently genuine C private and family Ready
checked_invariants.assessment: Ordering is visible in the intended typed source path, but end-to-end proof remains blocked by declared genuine C Ready integration.
checked_invariants.reasoning: B physical protection requires independently validated C Published installation SQL, C root and retained CAS proof. Family publication requires B Protected plus C protection. The source writer calls through genuine private/family Ready revalidation; OwnedReadyData::new still refuses a new companion. This is an unfinished prerequisite, not a bypass or permission to remove guards.

checked_invariants.invariant: B mapping/header/scalars/claim/receipt/Ready commit atomically, with separate Published
checked_invariants.assessment: Transaction structure is source-supported; first deletion insertion is broken by C13-CR-002.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The low-level atom performs all B inserts and exact transition CAS in the caller's FK-enabled transaction and requires prospective interpretation. The managed writer rolls back atom/prospective failures within nested scopes. Successful Ready closes/readback precede a distinct Published writer iteration.

checked_invariants.invariant: Retained physical pins span writers, closes and fresh readback; failed close/ACK permits no next SQL/FS probe
checked_invariants.assessment: Retention and normal success ordering are source-supported; the ACK stop contract is violated by C13-CR-001.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The witness borrows the complete image/closed publication and owns PublishedCasProof. During source publication the witness is borrowed throughout both commits and readbacks. Actual close errors use Cleanup and propagate; a standalone observer ACK error inside the new B owner snapshot needs strict propagation.

checked_invariants.invariant: Exact replay does not adopt partial state, and recovery does not manufacture authority
checked_invariants.assessment: Source-supported for the inspected DATA and writer routes; declared restart ownership restrictions remain.
checked_invariants.reasoning: Absent/reservation/protected are exact classifications; orphan membership, changed fixed remaining and partial roots refuse. Same-phase exact row replay returns AlreadyPresent; Published skips the writer loop. Physical protection reopening still requires actual original Staging and terminal retry requires the retained owner until a separate recovery owner exists.

checked_invariants.invariant: Autonomous C relies on its own protection, with explicit retained-source namespace classification
checked_invariants.assessment: Own-C authority separation is source-supported; aggregate source-root allocation is defective (C13-CR-003), and corruption cases remain unexecuted.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The new source namespace is parsed rather than excluded by prefix. Reservation-only/unowned source entries refuse. Callers compare retained source DATA to the C binding/union and independently validate C roots, journals and charged sets. These functions do not open B's database or native paths. No claim is made that source-only review exhaustively establishes every foreign-group corruption case.

The existing schema8 provider-evidence and admitted schema9/10 reclamation refusals remain. The new source functions reserve/protect/classify but do not release reservations, delete roots or weaken maintenance admission.

checked_invariants.assessment: No additional definite borrow/type/visibility defect established by this source inspection; not a typecheck.
checked_invariants.reasoning: The examined projection-visible proof accessors and context borrows provide source-level paths for the new cross-module calls. Unwired complete-image lease integration is already declared and is not counted as an invented compiler failure.

documentation_corrections.issue: The phrase 'actual successful OS SQLite close' overstates what WriterCloseObserver observes.
documentation_corrections.correction: Describe an ACK refusal after a successful SQLite connection close (Connection::close / sqlite3_close result). Do not infer independent OS file-handle-close evidence.
documentation_corrections.status: Acknowledged wording correction only; document left unchanged.

documentation_corrections.issue: Authored prospective recipe; no actual close-failure experiment was performed by this review.
documentation_corrections.correction: Keep it explicitly prospective and separate from ACK injection. A future busy sqlite3_close failure must not be described as an observed OS handle-close failure without separate evidence.

unresolved_evidence: Compilation/typechecking and runtime behavior remain unperformed. Formatting/self-review reports in the bundle were not treated as compiler or independent runtime evidence.

A genuine companion-capable OwnedReadyData/ManagedPrivateReady/ManagedFamilyReady route and a retained complete-image/source/remote-authority lease are still missing. Existing strict guards were not weakened in the inspected routes.

The new B publication/protection routes therefore do not establish a completed end-to-end C13 conversion. Findings about those routes are concrete source defects in the proposed implementation, not claims that the active native runner reached them.

Initial physical source protection reopening is limited to actual B Staging; terminal retry needs the retained original owner until a separately authenticated recovery owner exists. These are acknowledged limitations, not new findings.
No C14 durable-denied schema is delivered. This was not reclassified as a source-B defect.

Rollback atomicity under injected failures, zero-mutation replay, exact-capacity boundaries, foreign-group corruption, later capture coexistence and offline C autonomy were traced in source but not experimentally established.
The report does not authorize weakening C Ready/lease prerequisites, fixes, deployment, release, reclamation or further delegation. Those decisions remain with ROOT.
